from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):

        # 1. Setup layout with title and lecture lines
        title = "The Hook: The Alchemist's Dilemma"
        lines = [
            "Meet Leo and his two random magic jars.",
            "Jar A drops X coins; Jar B drops Y coins.",
            "We need the probability that their sum equals four."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)
        
        # Colors from storyboard and visual logic
        COLOR_A = "#ADD8E6"
        COLOR_B = "#FFD700"
        COLOR_POTION = "#FF69B4"
        COLOR_TEXT = "#FFFFFF"

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight first lecture line and introduce magic jars
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(COLOR_A))
        
        # Create Jar A icon representation
        jar_a_rect = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.0, width=0.8, color=COLOR_A)
        jar_a_text = Text("Jar A", font_size=24, color=COLOR_A)
        jar_a = VGroup(jar_a_rect, jar_a_text).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Create Jar B icon representation
        jar_b_rect = RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.0, width=0.8, color=COLOR_B)
        jar_b_text = Text("Jar B", font_size=24, color=COLOR_B)
        jar_b = VGroup(jar_b_rect, jar_b_text).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.1)
        
        # Position jars on the grid (B2 and B4 are side-by-side)
        self.place_at_grid(jar_a, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(jar_b, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(jar_a), FadeIn(jar_b))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight second line and show the goal: a potion costing 4 coins
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(COLOR_B))
        
        # Potion bottle representation using a triangle and a small top
        potion_body = Triangle(color=COLOR_POTION, fill_opacity=0.3).scale(0.8)
        potion_cork = Square(side_length=0.15, color=COLOR_POTION, fill_opacity=1).next_to(potion_body, UP, buff=0)
        potion_label = Text("4 Coins", font_size=18, color=WHITE).move_to(potion_body.get_center() + DOWN*0.1)
        potion = VGroup(potion_body, potion_cork, potion_label)
        
        # Position potion below the jars (D3)
        self.place_at_grid(potion, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Define X and Y labels for jars
        label_x = MathTex("X", color=COLOR_A, font_size=36).next_to(jar_a, UP, buff=0.2)
        label_y = MathTex("Y", color=COLOR_B, font_size=36).next_to(jar_b, UP, buff=0.2)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(potion), Write(label_x), Write(label_y))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Highlight third line and show the mathematical goal
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(COLOR_POTION))
        
        # Fade in the sum question text between the jars and the potion
        sum_text = Text("Jar A + Jar B =?", font_size=24, color=COLOR_TEXT)
        # Position at C3 (above potion, below/between jars)
        self.place_at_grid(sum_text, "C3", scale_factor=0.8)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title = "Prerequisite Check: Independence & PDFs"
        lines = [
            "Assume these jars act independently of each other.",
            "Each jar's uncertainty is described by a PDF.",
            "Their joint probability is the product of individual PDFs."
        ]
        
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#A9A9A9")
        
        # Visualizing Jars A and B
        # Since no Asset tags were provided, we use a simple container representation
        jar_a = VGroup(
            RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.2, width=0.8, color="#A9A9A9"),
            Text("Jar A", font_size=18, color="#FFFFFF").shift(UP * 0.8)
        )
        jar_b = VGroup(
            RoundedRectangle(corner_radius=0.1, height=1.2, width=0.8, color="#A9A9A9"),
            Text("Jar B", font_size=18, color="#FFFFFF").shift(UP * 0.8)
        )
        
        self.place_at_grid(jar_a, "B2", scale_factor=0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(jar_b, "B5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Dashed line between jars representing independence/separation
        dashed_line = DashedLine(
            start=self.grid["B3"],
            end=self.grid["B4"],
            color="#A9A9A9"
        )
        
        self.play(Create(jar_a), Create(jar_b), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(Create(dashed_line), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00") # Matching the first curve color
        
        # Bell curve function: f(x) = exp(-x^2)
        def bell_curve(x):
            return np.exp(-x**2)
        
        # Green PDF for Jar A
        axes_a = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[0, 1.2], x_length=1.5, y_length=1.0, 
                      axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": "#A9A9A9"}).scale(0.7)
        curve_a = axes_a.plot(bell_curve, color="#00FF00")
        label_a = MathTex("f(x)", font_size=20, color="#00FF00").next_to(axes_a, UP, buff=0.1)
        pdf_a = VGroup(axes_a, curve_a, label_a)
        
        # Blue PDF for Jar B
        axes_b = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[0, 1.2], x_length=1.5, y_length=1.0, 
                      axis_config={"include_tip": False, "color": "#A9A9A9"}).scale(0.7)
        curve_b = axes_b.plot(bell_curve, color="#00BFFF")
        label_b = MathTex("g(y)", font_size=20, color="#00BFFF").next_to(axes_b, UP, buff=0.1)
        pdf_b = VGroup(axes_b, curve_b, label_b)
        
        self.place_at_grid(pdf_a, "D2", scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(pdf_b, "D5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Create(pdf_a), run_time=1.0)
        self.play(Create(pdf_b), run_time=1.0)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Joint probability formula
        joint_formula = MathTex(
            "P(X, Y) = f(x) \\cdot g(y)",
            font_size=32,
            color="#FFFFFF"
        )
        
        # Position formula in the lower central area of the grid
        self.place_in_area(joint_formula, "F2", "F5", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        self.play(Write(joint_formula), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(Indicate(joint_formula, color="#FFFFFF"))
        self.wait(2.0)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        # Section data
        title = "The Geometric Intuition of Z = X + Y"
        lines = [
            "Let the sum Z equal a constant value z.",
            "This equation forms a diagonal line on the plane.",
            "To find P(Z=z), we scan this specific line.",
            "We accumulate joint probabilities along this diagonal path.",
            "This scan explains how the sum's distribution emerges."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title, lines)

        # Colors (L008: Hex codes)
        COLOR_Z = "#FFFFFF"
        COLOR_LINE = "#FFFF00"
        COLOR_PULSE = "#FF4500"
        COLOR_BARS = "#FFFFFF"
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Let the sum Z equal a constant value z.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(COLOR_Z)
        
        eq_z = MathTex("Z = X + Y = z", color=COLOR_Z)
        self.place_at_grid(eq_z, "A3", scale_factor=0.9)
        self.play(Write(eq_z))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # This equation forms a diagonal line on the plane.
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(COLOR_LINE)
        self.wait(1.5) # L010: Absorption time
        
        # Plane area: B2 to F6 (L002: Start visuals at Col 2 or right)
        plane = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=4,
            axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": "#FFFFFF"}, # L001: axis_config instead of hide_tip
            background_line_style={"stroke_color": "#444444", "stroke_width": 1}
        )
        self.place_in_area(plane, "B2", "F6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        # Labels (L002: Scaled and close to objects)
        x_label = MathTex("X", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(x_label, "D6", scale_factor=0.8)
        x_label.shift(RIGHT * 0.3)
        
        y_label = MathTex("Y", font_size=24, color="#FFFFFF")
        self.place_at_grid(y_label, "B4", scale_factor=0.8)
        y_label.shift(UP * 0.3)

        z_val = ValueTracker(2.0)
        
        def get_line():
            z = z_val.get_value()
            # x + y = z constraint within [0, 4] bounds
            x_start = max(0, z - 4)
            x_end = min(z, 4)
            
            if x_start >= x_end:
                # Minimal segment if at the very corner
                p = plane.coords_to_point(x_start, z - x_start)
                return Line(p, p + RIGHT * 0.01, color=COLOR_LINE)
                
            p1 = plane.coords_to_point(x_start, z - x_start)
            p2 = plane.coords_to_point(x_end, z - x_end)
            return Line(p1, p2, color=COLOR_LINE, stroke_width=4)

        diag_line = always_redraw(get_line)
        
        self.play(Create(plane), Write(x_label), Write(y_label))
        self.play(Create(diag_line))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # To find P(Z=z), we scan this specific line.
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(COLOR_PULSE)
        self.wait(1.5) # L010: Absorption time
        
        # L004: Using Indicate
        self.play(Indicate(diag_line, color=COLOR_PULSE, scale_factor=1.1))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # We accumulate joint probabilities along this diagonal path.
        self.lecture[2].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[3].set_color(COLOR_LINE)
        self.wait(1.5) # L010: Absorption time
        
        # Animate the yellow line sliding across the plane.
        self.play(z_val.animate.set_value(0.2), run_time=1.2)
        self.play(z_val.animate.set_value(3.8), run_time=3.5, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # This scan explains how the sum's distribution emerges.
        self.lecture[3].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[4].set_color(COLOR_BARS)
        self.wait(1.5) # L010: Absorption time
        
        # Show vertical white bars rising from the moving line.
        h_factor = ValueTracker(0)
        
        # L027/L011: Minimal number of mobjects in always_redraw
        def get_bars():
            z = z_val.get_value()
            hf = h_factor.get_value()
            bars = VGroup()
            if z <= 0 or hf <= 0: return bars
            
            num_bars = 7
            x_start = max(0, z - 4)
            x_end = min(z, 4)
            
            if x_end <= x_start: return bars

            for i in range(num_bars):
                x = x_start + (x_end - x_start) * (i / (num_bars - 1))
                y = z - x
                base = plane.coords_to_point(x, y)
                # Joint probability metaphor (Gaussian peak at center 2,2)
                prob = np.exp(-((x-2)**2 + (y-2)**2)/2)
                bar_height = prob * 1.5 * hf
                if bar_height > 0.05:
                    bar = Line(base, base + UP * bar_height, color=COLOR_BARS, stroke_width=4)
                    bars.add(bar)
            return bars

        bars_group = always_redraw(get_bars)
        self.add(bars_group)
        
        # Reset and scan with rising bars
        self.play(
            z_val.animate.set_value(0.5),
            h_factor.animate.set_value(1),
            run_time=2
        )
        self.play(z_val.animate.set_value(4.0), run_time=4, rate_func=linear)
        
        self.wait(2.0)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout(
            "The Convolution Formula: Flip and Slide", 
            [
                "The convolution formula mathematically defines this diagonal scan.",
                "First, we flip one distribution to reflect it.",
                "Next, we slide it across the other distribution.",
                "The overlap area at each step gives the sum.",
                "This 'flip and slide' creates the new distribution's shape."
            ]
        )

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Highlight lecture line 1
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00") # Highlighting with Yellow
        
        formula = MathTex(
            r"(f * g)(z) = \int_{-\infty}^{\infty} f(x)g(z - x) \, dx",
            color="#FFFFFF"
        )
        self.place_in_area(formula, "A2", "B6", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        self.play(Write(formula))
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Reset color and highlight line 2
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")

        # Visual elements: Two squares (Uniform Distributions)
        # f(x) is green, g(x) is magenta
        # Position them on a shared axis
        axes = NumberPlane(
            x_range=[-2, 3, 1],
            y_range=[0, 1.5, 1],
            x_length=4,
            y_length=2,
            axis_config={"include_tip": False} # Lesson L001
        ).add_coordinates()
        self.place_in_area(axes, "C2", "E6", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        f_square = Rectangle(
            width=1, height=1, 
            fill_color="#00FF00", fill_opacity=0.5, 
            stroke_color="#00FF00"
        ).move_to(axes.c2p(0.5, 0.5))
        
        g_square = Rectangle(
            width=1, height=1, 
            fill_color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.5, 
            stroke_color="#FF00FF"
        ).move_to(axes.c2p(0.5, 0.5))
        
        f_label = MathTex("f(x)", color="#00FF00").scale(0.7)
        g_label = MathTex("g(x)", color="#FF00FF").scale(0.7)
        f_label.next_to(f_square, UP, buff=0.1)
        g_label.next_to(g_square, UP, buff=0.1)

        self.play(Create(axes))
        self.play(FadeIn(f_square), FadeIn(f_label))
        self.wait(1.0)
        
        # Flipping g(x) to g(-x)
        # Rotate around its center then move to the reflected position
        self.play(FadeIn(g_square), FadeIn(g_label))
        self.play(
            Rotate(g_square, axis=UP, angle=PI),
            g_square.animate.move_to(axes.c2p(-0.5, 0.5)),
            g_label.animate.set_text("g(-x)").move_to(axes.c2p(-0.5, 1.2))
        )
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Reset color and highlight line 3
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FF00FF")

        # sliding g(z-x)
        z_tracker = ValueTracker(-1.0)
        
        # Updaters for sliding g square
        def update_g(mob):
            z = z_tracker.get_value()
            # z-x for x in [0,1] is [-1, 0] shifted by z
            mob.move_to(axes.c2p(z - 0.5, 0.5))
            
        g_square.add_updater(update_g)
        g_label.add_updater(lambda mob: mob.move_to(g_square.get_top() + UP * 0.2))

        self.play(z_tracker.animate.set_value(0.0), run_time=1.5)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        # Reset color and highlight line 4
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFE0")

        # Overlap tracker
        overlap_rect = Rectangle(
            fill_color="#FFFFE0", fill_opacity=0.8, stroke_width=0
        )
        
        def update_overlap(mob):
            z = z_tracker.get_value()
            # f(x) is on [0, 1]. g(z-x) is on [z-1, z].
            # Intersection is [max(0, z-1), min(1, z)]
            left = max(0, z-1)
            right = min(1, z)
            if left < right:
                width = right - left
                center_x = (left + right) / 2
                mob.stretch_to_fit_width(width * (axes.c2p(1,0)[0] - axes.c2p(0,0)[0]))
                mob.stretch_to_fit_height(1 * (axes.c2p(0,1)[1] - axes.c2p(0,0)[1]))
                mob.move_to(axes.c2p(center_x, 0.5))
                mob.set_opacity(0.8)
            else:
                mob.set_opacity(0)

        overlap_rect.add_updater(update_overlap)
        self.add(overlap_rect)

        # Slide through overlap
        self.play(z_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0), run_time=3.0, rate_func=linear)
        self.wait(1.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        # Reset color and highlight line 5
        self.lecture[3].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.lecture[4].set_color("#00FFFF")

        # Drawing the resulting triangle
        # Area(z) = z for 0<z<1, 2-z for 1<z<2
        triangle_points = [
            axes.c2p(0, 0),
            axes.c2p(1, 1),
            axes.c2p(2, 0)
        ]
        result_triangle = Polygon(*triangle_points, color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        result_label = MathTex("(f*g)(z)", color="#00FFFF").scale(0.8)
        self.place_at_grid(result_label, "F4", scale_factor=0.8)

        # Reset z and draw triangle as we slide
        g_square.remove_updater(update_g)
        g_label.remove_updater(g_label.updaters[0])
        overlap_rect.remove_updater(update_overlap)
        self.remove(overlap_rect)
        
        z_tracker.set_value(0.0)
        g_square.move_to(axes.c2p(-0.5, 0.5))
        
        # New updater to trace the triangle
        result_trace = VMobject(color="#00FFFF", stroke_width=4)
        result_trace.set_points_as_corners([axes.c2p(0, 0)])

        def update_trace(mob):
            z = z_tracker.get_value()
            if 0 <= z <= 1:
                val = z
            elif 1 < z <= 2:
                val = 2 - z
            else:
                val = 0
            
            new_point = axes.c2p(z, val)
            mob.add_points_as_corners([new_point])

        g_square.add_updater(update_g)
        result_trace.add_updater(update_trace)
        self.add(result_trace)

        self.play(
            z_tracker.animate.set_value(2.0),
            FadeIn(result_label),
            run_time=3.0,
            rate_func=linear
        )
        
        self.wait(2.0)

        # Cleanup updaters
        g_square.remove_updater(update_g)
        result_trace.remove_updater(update_trace)

class Section6Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        title_text = "Summary & Key Takeaway"
        lecture_lines = [
            "Adding variables means summing probabilities along diagonal lines.",
            "Convolution is the engine driving this mathematical transformation.",
            "It explains why the bell curve appears everywhere."
        ]
        self.setup_layout(title_text, lecture_lines)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show the yellow diagonal line (#FFFF00) on a 2D plane. self.wait(1.5).
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Create a coordinate system
        # L001 precaution: manage tips in constructor
        axes = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1],
            y_range=[0, 4, 1],
            x_length=3,
            y_length=3,
            axis_config={
                "color": "#FFFFFF",
                "stroke_width": 2,
                "include_tip": True,
            }
        )
        
        # Diagonal line: x + y = 3
        diag_line = Line(
            start=axes.c2p(3, 0),
            end=axes.c2p(0, 3),
            color="#FFFF00",
            stroke_width=6
        )
        
        diag_visual = VGroup(axes, diag_line)
        # L002: Place visuals starting at Column 2 or further right
        self.place_in_area(diag_visual, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.9)
        
        self.play(Create(axes), run_time=1)
        self.play(Create(diag_line), run_time=1)
        self.wait(1.5) # L010: Absorption time

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Display 'f * g' in cyan (#00FFFF) with a glowing effect. self.wait(1.5).
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        # Formula for convolution
        conv_formula = MathTex(r"(f * g)(z)", color="#00FFFF")
        # L002: Scale primary labels to 0.7-0.8 or appropriate for grid area
        self.place_in_area(conv_formula, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=1.4)
        
        self.play(FadeOut(diag_visual))
        self.play(Write(conv_formula))
        # L004: "Glowing effect" using Indicate
        self.play(Indicate(conv_formula, color="#00FFFF", scale_factor=1.2))
        self.wait(1.5) # L010: Absorption time

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Show a sequence: Square -> Triangle -> Bell Curve (#FFFFFF). self.wait(2.0).
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # Shapes for the transformation sequence (L009 morphing anchors)
        square = Square(side_length=2, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        self.place_in_area(square, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # Triangle (Irwin-Hall distribution for n=2)
        tri_points = [
            square.get_corner(DL),
            square.get_corner(DR),
            square.get_top()
        ]
        triangle = Polygon(*tri_points, color="#FFFFFF", fill_opacity=0.3)
        
        # Bell Curve (Normal distribution / Irwin-Hall for large n)
        # L027: Not using updaters or thousands of objects here
        bell_curve = FunctionGraph(
            lambda x: 1.8 * np.exp(-1.5 * x**2),
            x_range=[-2, 2],
            color="#FFFFFF"
        )
        # Shift bell curve to match the area center
        self.place_in_area(bell_curve, "B2", "E5", scale_factor=0.8)
        # Adjust vertical position slightly for visual balance
        bell_curve.shift(DOWN * 0.5)

        self.play(FadeOut(conv_formula))
        self.play(Create(square))
        self.wait(1.0)
        
        # L009: Morphing transformations
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(square, triangle))
        self.wait(1.0)
        
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(triangle, bell_curve))
        self.wait(2.0) # L010: Final absorption time

outline.topic: Adding Random Variables and Convolution in Probability
outline.target_audience: Undergraduate students in STEM fields (Mathematics, Engineering, Data Science)

sections.title: The Hook: The Alchemist's Dilemma
sections.content: Introduce the motivation for adding random variables. Use a character-driven scenario to explain why we need to find the probability distribution of a sum rather than just the sum of means. Explain that when we combine two independent random sources, the resulting uncertainty 'spreads' in a specific way.
sections.example: Leo the Alchemist has two magic jars. Jar A (Variable X) drops 1 to 3 gold coins randomly. Jar B (Variable Y) drops 1 to 3 gold coins randomly. To buy a potion costing 4 coins, Leo needs to know the probability of X + Y = 4. Simply adding the average outcomes isn't enough; we need the full distribution of the sum Z.

sections.title: Prerequisite Check: Independence & PDFs
sections.content: Briefly define the two pillars needed for convolution: 1. Independence (the outcome of X doesn't affect Y). 2. Probability Density Functions (PDFs), visualized as the 'shape' of uncertainty. Use a simple 2D coordinate system (X-axis and Y-axis) to show how two independent variables create a joint probability space.
sections.example: Visualizing two bell curves on separate axes. For independence, the joint probability P(X, Y) is simply the product of their individual probabilities: f(x) * g(y). This creates a 'probability landscape' over a flat plane.

sections.title: The Geometric Intuition of Z = X + Y
sections.content: Transition to the sum Z. On the X-Y plane, the equation X + Y = z represents a diagonal line. To find the probability of a specific sum 'z', we must accumulate all the joint probabilities along that specific diagonal line. This sets the stage for the integral/summation formula.
sections.example: An animation showing a diagonal 'scanner beam' (the line x + y = z) sliding across the X-Y plane. As the beam moves, it collects the 'height' of the joint probability landscape at every point it touches.

sections.title: The Convolution Formula: Flip and Slide
sections.content: Introduce the Convolution formula: (f * g)(z) = ∫ f(x)g(z - x) dx. Break this down visually into three steps: 1. Flip (reflecting g(x) to get g(-x)), 2. Shift (sliding it by z), and 3. Multiply/Integrate (finding the area of overlap). This 'Flip and Slide' is the heart of convolution.
sections.example: Visualizing two rectangular blocks (Uniform Distributions). As one rectangle slides across the other, the area of their overlap starts at zero, grows linearly to a peak, and then decreases, forming a triangle shape.

sections.title: Application: The Central Limit Theorem Preview
sections.content: Show what happens when we keep adding more variables. Convolution 'smooths' the distribution. Demonstrate that adding two uniform (square) distributions creates a triangle, and adding a third creates a bell-like curve. This bridges the gap to the Central Limit Theorem.
sections.example: Three robots are throwing darts. Robot 1's error is a square wave. Robot 2's is a square wave. Their combined error (convolution) is a triangle. When Robot 3 (another square wave) joins, the total error distribution becomes a smooth 'Spline' that looks almost like a Normal Distribution.

sections.title: Summary & Key Takeaway
sections.content: Recap the logic: Adding variables involves summing joint probabilities along a diagonal. For independent variables, this process is mathematically defined as Convolution. Emphasize that Convolution is the tool that explains why the world tends toward 'Normal' (Gaussian) distributions.
sections.example: A final graphic showing the transformation: [Square + Square] -> [Triangle] -> [Bell Curve]. The formula (f * g)(z) is the 'engine' driving this transformation.
